subject: Demo follow-up: feature-level econ asks + budget envelope
messages:
From: Alicia Park <apark@carebridge.ai>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from demo + rough usage / budget

Thanks again for the product walkthrough today — the team found the latency and cost controls promising. I promised a quick summary of the numbers we discussed on the call so you have something concrete to work from. High level: CareBridge is evaluating embedding/search + two generation features (summary + conversational triage).

Quick usage sketch (monthly):
- Active users: ~25k MAU (pilot), ramp to 75k in 12 months
- Feature breakdown:
  - Symptom summary (avg 750 tokens/request) — 120k requests/month
  - Conversational triage (avg 1,600 tokens/session, multi-turn) — 240k sessions/month (~2.8M tokens/session total)
  - Semantic search embeddings (1 embedding per session, 768-d) — 360k embeddings/month
- Rough monthly token volume today: ~40M tokens, potentially 150M at scale

Budget and economics guidance from our side:
- We internally expect a target infrastructure budget in the pilot of $12k–$20k/month for inference (excluding infra + support) — that translates roughly to a target of $300–$500 per 1M tokens depending on model choice.
- Commercial goal: we want feature-level clarity (i.e., $/feature and expected margin net of service fees). CAC: we need to keep payback under 9 months for features tied to signup flows.

Could you send a simple per-feature unit-econ sketch and a range for $/1M tokens with assumptions (model family, quantization, caching, and latency SLO) so we can validate vs our internal budget? Also please confirm what additional data you need from us (e.g., session length distributions, annotation samples).

Thanks — Alicia
Alicia Park
Head of Product, CareBridge
apark@carebridge.ai

Attachment: carebridge-usage-estimates.pdf (1 page CSV summary)

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Alicia Park <apark@carebridge.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo + rough usage / budget

Alicia — great notes, thanks for the clarity. Reposting to our internal econ owners (Ben, Karthik) and including a quick next-steps plan below. We attached a first-pass workbook (econ-workbook-v1.xlsx) showing a couple of scenarios by model family (Llama2-13B quantized FP16, Mistral-7B q4) and caching assumptions.

Immediate ask (what we'll deliver by EOD tomorrow):
- Per-feature $/month and $/1M tokens range (low / mid / high) with explicit assumptions: model, quantization, avg tokens per request, caching hit rate, and GPU type.
- CAC payback sensitivity: compute months-to-payback for 3 acquisition cost points (low/med/high) and two pricing approaches (subscription vs per-feature usage).
- Margin sensitivity table showing gross margin vs inference cost (0–40%).

Assumptions I want to confirm before we lock numbers:
- Symptom summary: 750 tokens avg (you listed) — confirm distribution (p50/p90)
- Triage sessions: 1,600 tokens avg across session, is that per session or per turn?
- Embeddings: vector dim and expected indexing frequency (you said 1 per session)

Ben and Karthik — can you validate the attached workbook assumptions (esp. cache hit rate and per-token costs for the two model families) and add any notes on potential dedicated capacity discounts if they want guaranteed latency?

Alicia — we'll send the initial per-feature numbers tomorrow and flag any tradeoffs that materially change the unit math (e.g., multi-turn KV cache reuse vs fresh tokens each turn).

-jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: econ-workbook-v1.xlsx (workbook with pivot tables and scenario tabs)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo + rough usage / budget

Quick notes on workbook assumptions — I added comments in the file, but high-level callouts here:
- Model assumptions: use Mistral-7B q4 for the low-cost baseline (~$220–260 /1M tokens with aggressive caching and batching) and Llama2-13B int8 for mid-tier (~$380–$520 /1M) — numbers assume continuous batching at modest QPS; if they need sub-200ms tail latency we'll need dedicated nodes and that moves the cost ~20–40% up.
- Cache reuse: for triage the KV cache reuse rate is critical; if they have 3–4 turns with the same context we can effectively drop per-turn cost by ~35% in our model. Need session turn distribution from CareBridge to firm this up.
- CAC/payback: to keep payback <=9 months we need either a subscription component (~$3–5/user/mo) or a higher per-feature monetization (>$0.30 per triage session) — I added a scenario sheet for both.

I'll push an updated workbook with scenario IDs (S1/S2/S3) and a short narrative. Karthik — any additional engineering constraints or discounts to call out?

-Ben
Ben Carter
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Alicia Park <apark@carebridge.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo + rough usage / budget

Alicia — attached is our initial per-feature sketch (S1 low-cost / S2 mid / S3 high). Summary highlights:
- Symptom summary: $/1M tokens = $210 (S1) / $410 (S2) / $790 (S3). Assumes caching only for repeated prefix prompts and LLM family variations noted in the workbook.
- Conversational triage: $/1M tokens = $260 (S1) / $480 (S2) / $900 (S3). Significant delta driven by latency SLO and multi-turn cache reuse.
- Embeddings: priced separately per 1k vectors — ballpark $0.50–$1.10 per 1k depending on dimension and index refresh cadence.

CAC/payback (pilot assumptions):
- If you price triage as part of onboarding conversion (one-off revenue) we estimate 6–9 months payback at a $120 CAC and mid-tier pricing; if you rely solely on usage-based revenue, payback extends toward 12+ months unless you keep per-feature prices in the mid-to-high band.

Next steps I propose (pick 2):
1) You share session turn histograms (p50/p90) and any SLO constraints (tail latency target).
2) We run a short pilot with a fixed monthly token commitment to lock in a mid-tier $/1M token and gather real-turn reuse numbers. Pilot pricing can be structured as a hybrid (monthly minimum + usage overage).
3) If you'd like, we can prepare a draft commercial term sheet with a 6-month commitment for mid-tier pricing and a clause for capacity-based discounts.

Would appreciate confirmation of which next step you'd prefer and any constraints on contract length or procurement timelines. If helpful, we can set up a 30-min follow-up tomorrow to walk through the workbook together.

Thanks — jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Quoted attachments: econ-workbook-v1.xlsx (updated scenario comments), carebridge-usage-estimates.pdf
